title: Cache warmup SLAs & OSS integration brainstorm
content:
Meeting: informal brainstorm / post-standup sync
Date: 2027-03-08
Attendees: Asha (notes), Liam, Maya, Diego, Priya
Purpose: Sketch a pragmatic approach for guaranteeing cold-start SLAs via a cache-warmup pattern and explore how we open-source a minimal warmup library for external customers. Keep notes rough — this is a working doc.

High-level problem statement
- Production symptom: new model instances (Dedicated and Private) show a 3–7x token-latency spike for the first few user sessions because KV caches are cold and prefill/coalescing doesn't have enough upstream signals.
- Business need: minimize first-byte latency for interactive apps (chat) to meet p95 SLOs for enterprise customers that have stricter SLAs.
- Constraints: warmup must not blow GPU memory or waste tokens; must be safe in multi-tenant Dedicated pools; must be optional for Private deployments with limited ops resources.

Goals for this initiative
1) Define a small set of warmup SLAs (p95,p99) for targeted routes (chat-start, streaming-init).
2) Implement a light-weight warmup orchestration that can run in the control plane or a small envoy-sidecar for Private.
3) Provide an OSS library (python client) that customers can embed in startup hooks or sidecars to prime caches with synthetically generated prefixes.
4) Instrument and measure cost impact (tokens, GPU cycles) and model quality drift risk.
5) Provide fallbacks when warmup fails (graceful degraded responses / early fallback to smaller model).

Notes from the technical deep dive
- Warmup signal types:
  - Prefix synthetic prompts derived from user prompts (e.g., default greetings, domain-specific first-turn prompts).
  - Replay of recent real requests (from shadow logs) — requires privacy/consent controls.
  - Minimal prefix playbooks: 1–3 short tokens to populate the KV attention layers enough to avoid cache miss storms.

- Where to run warmup:
  - Control-plane orchestrated batch to GPU nodes on container launch (hosted/dedicated). Pros: centralized, can schedule to avoid peak. Cons: control plane footprint and security considerations.
  - Sidecar preflight within node (Private): pros: local, no extra network hop. Cons: resource contention with serving process.
  - Worker-job off the serving device that walks through a lightweight tracing-only codepath (no heavy sampling).

- Warmup intensity knobs:
  - prefix_length (tokens): 4–32 tokens explored. Lower tends to warm latent KVs; higher increases token cost.
  - concurrency: number of parallel warmup sessions per instance (1–8).
  - kv_prefill_mode: "shallow" vs "deep" — shallow uses short prefixes across many prompt templates, deep uses longer in-domain prompts.
  - budget_cap: per-instance token cap per minute to bound cost.

- Safety & privacy:
  - For replayed requests, mask PII and require customer opt-in. Add a policy flag for Private.
  - Warmup payloads should never be logged at full granularity; use hashed telemetry.

Experiment plan (next 2 sprints)
Sprint A (two weeks):
- Implement a minimal control-plane warmup runner prototype that invokes model inference with a shallow prefix (6 tokens) for new container starts.
- Metrics to capture: cold-start p50/p95 latency, tokens consumed, GPU utilization spike profile, and kv-hit-rate for first 30s.
- Small canary on staging: 10% of new instances across two skewed workloads (chat-heavy, embedding-batch).
- Owners: Diego (runner), Maya (metrics), Liam (safety).

Sprint B (two weeks):
- Add railings: budget_cap enforcement + dynamic backoff if overall cluster load > threshold.
- Introduce an OSS python library stub and an example sidecar recipe for Private deployments.
- Validate privacy mask on replay path.
- Owners: Asha (OSS readme + examples), Priya (sidecar config), Diego (backoff).

Success criteria (measurable)
- p95 cold-start latency for chat-init decreases to < 1.8x warm baseline (goal: <1.5x) across canary workloads.
- Token overhead per instance < 120 tokens within the first 60 seconds.
- Rolling warmup does not increase steady-state latency or tail within 5% of baseline.
- No privacy incidents in replay tests (PII masked).

Risks and unknowns
- Warmup may thrash KV eviction policies — need careful tuning of prefill size.
- Dedicated pools with strict GPU reservations might see degraded throughput if warmup runs without pacing.
- OSS consumers might misuse warmup (heavy prefill) causing higher costs; need sensible defaults and instrumentation.

Open design questions (to resolve in design doc)
- Should warmup run on every container start or only on the first request for a model version? (tradeoff: repeated starts vs coverage).
- How to express warmup budgets in billing terms for Dedicated customers? (token vs time-based?)
- Can we provide a warmup ML model that predicts best minimal prefixes per customer workload to reduce tokens?

Proposed API & config sketch (working, terse)
- control_plane_warmup: {enabled: bool, prefix_templates: [str], prefix_length: int, concurrency: int, budget_tokens: int, kv_prefill_mode: "shallow"|"deep"}
- oss-client example: RedwoodWarmupClient(init_templates=["Hello","Start chat:"], token_budget=100)
- sidecar: warmup.enabled=true, run_on_startup=true, max_parallel=2, backoff_throttle_pct=70

Telemetry and observability needs
- New metrics: warmup.tokens_used, warmup.start_ts, warmup.finish_ts, warmup.kv_hit_delta, warmup.failed_runs, warmup.backoff_count
- Dashboards: warmup cost vs p95 latency delta over time, per-customer warmup impact, warmup-induced GPU spikes graph (per-host).
- Alerts: warmup.failed_runs > 5% over 15m AND cluster_load > 80% -> disable warmup auto.

Action items (owners & due dates)
- Diego: prototype control-plane runner + canary harness by 2027-03-22 (JIRA-RT-4123).
- Maya: add warmup metrics to kube-exporter and create initial dashboard by 2027-03-24.
- Asha: draft OSS README and example sidecar repo skeleton by 2027-03-24.
- Priya: compile privacy masking checklist and review replay policy by 2027-03-18.
- Liam: evaluate memory eviction telemetry and propose safety thresholds by 2027-03-19.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Consider an optional "warmup-lite" that only populates first-layer KV (faster, cheaper).
- Could leverage existing caching hints from routing (e.g., route metadata = "warmup-templates") to avoid per-customer config explosion.
- If OSS takes off, provide a hosted template library (domain packs) with community contributions.

Next sync
- Quick triage Tuesday standup (2027-03-09) to confirm owners and blockages.
- Demo prototype on March 22 canary run, brief synopsis in engineering weekly update.

Appendix: quick experiment notes (from yesterday's adhoc)
- shallow-prefix (6 tokens) across 5 containers: p95 latency drop from 3.7s -> 2.1s on chat-init; tokens consumed ~85 per container; observed transient 6% GPU util spike lasting 12s.
- deep-prefix (24 tokens) improved p95 to 1.6s but tokens consumed ~320 and triggered KV evictions on a heavily loaded host.

End of notes.

-- Asha
